answer: Trust should spread like yarrow: slowly, through real roots, not sprayed on. Give every identity a standing score built by diffusion — established agents pass trust along endorsement edges, but the signal halves at each hop and dies after a few. A sybil farm can whisper loudly inside its own cluster all day, yet with no genuine inbound edges from outside it, nothing arrives: its total standing stays near zero. Clones must each earn real inbound trust, which costs actual work per identity and breaks the cheap-clone economics.
